route_decision.before_m87: Goal4458 kept fused CPU/Numba fastest on 8192/16384/32768 bodies.
route_decision.after_m87: Large-scale current guidance is scale-dependent: fused Numba CUDA is fastest on 65536 and 131072 bodies, while fused CPU/Numba remains the small-scale fastest route from Goal4458.
route_decision.prepared_optix_status: Prepared RTDL/OptiX+Numba remains RT-core aggregate-frontier device-column evidence, but is not the fastest force-summary route at either M87 scale.

interpretation.headline: Barnes-Hut route guidance is scale-dependent after M87.
interpretation.why_numba_cuda_wins_large_rows: The fused Numba CUDA route keeps traversal and force accumulation in one no-C++ partner kernel and avoids aggregate-frontier row emission.
interpretation.why_prepared_optix_still_loses: The prepared OptiX route uses RT cores for generic aggregate-frontier device-column collection, but still pays the frontier-emission contract before partner vector accumulation; at 131072 bodies the frontier traversal median alone is about 0.594s.
interpretation.v3_implication: A competitive RT-core Barnes-Hut route needs a fused app-agnostic RT-native/device aggregate-vector primitive, not more tuning of the row-emission frontier contract.
